financials_interim.notes: Lanka Ashok Leyland PLC (ASHO), commercial vehicle assembly/distribution (Capital Goods), single-entity company -- the filing presents ONLY one set of statements (no 'Group'/'Company' split, no subsidiaries mentioned anywhere in the filing), so stored as a single GROUP-basis row per convention for single-entity filers. FYE 31 March. Quarter 01 FY2026/27 (three months ended 30 June 2026) vs Quarter 01 FY2025/26 (three months ended 30 June 2025) comparative, both explicitly presented on the face P&L (page 3). Revenue is broken out by product line: New Vehicle Sales 5,950,423,794 (2025: 2,831,976,091, +110%) is overwhelmingly the largest and fastest-growing line, driving nearly all of the Total Revenue increase; Spare Parts Sales 193,548,903 (2025: 72,510,256, +167%) grew fastest in percentage terms but off a small base; Vehicle Repair Income +14% to 93,557,880; Diesel Generator Set Sales -12% to 5,998,305; Vehicle Hiring Income -10% to 238,690,999 (2025: 264,194,666) was the only revenue line to decline. operating_profit=1,275,334,287 is the filing's own printed subtotal 'Profit before Interest and Tax' (Gross Profit 1,701,856,182 + Other Income 79,159,214 - Selling & Distribution Expenses 40,027,078 - Administrative Expenses 301,979,244 - Impairment Charge on Trade Receivables 86,545,840 - Other Operating Expenses 77,128,947 = 1,275,334,287). finance_costs=2,031,785, finance_income=57,918,277 -- both given as separate gross lines (unlike a purely net presentation), summing to Net Finance Income of 55,886,492, which the filing adds (not subtracts) to arrive at PBT: 1,275,334,287 + 55,886,492 = 1,331,220,779, ties exactly. tax_expense=397,301,718 (printed bracketed, a genuine expense both periods). profit_after_tax=933,919,061: PBT 1,331,220,779 - tax 397,301,718 = 933,919,061, ties exactly. eps_basic=257.93, only one EPS line given ('Basic and Diluted Earnings per Share'), eps_diluted mirrors it -- based on 3,620,843 shares in issue (Note 7, unchanged throughout, no rights issue or split this period); 933,919,061/3,620,843 = 257.93, ties exactly. trade_receivables=2,173,544,727 ('Trade and Other Receivables', current). NOTE: ASHO separately discloses 'Rental Receivable from Trade Debtors' (Non Current 269,134,314 + Current 465,735,763 = 734,870,077 total, per Note 11) relating to its vehicle-hiring/leasing book -- this is a DISTINCT receivable type from ordinary trade receivables and is deliberately excluded from the trade_receivables figure stored here (which captures only the 'Trade and Other Receivables' line) to avoid double-counting or conflating the two. trade_payables=4,478,396,520 ('Trade & Other Payables', current) -- this is unusually large relative to inventory (7,784,844,183) and likely reflects import-supplier financing given ASHO assembles/imports commercial vehicles (see FX note below). short_term_borrowings=206,366,122 = Bank Overdraft (current) only -- there is NO separate 'Interest Bearing Borrowings'/'Loans and borrowings' line anywhere on this balance sheet (current or non-current); Lease Liability (current 37,387,800 + non-current 36,392,108) is a distinct line kept OUT of borrowings per line-item discipline (consistent with treating operating/finance lease liabilities separately from interest-bearing debt). long_term_borrowings=0 (no non-current borrowings line at all). FX EXPOSURE (per task guidance -- vehicle assembly typically has imported-component costs): the cash flow statement's working-capital adjustments include an 'Unrealized Foreign Exchange Loss/(Gain)' item of 9,167,402 (an unrealised FX LOSS this quarter, vs a small gain of 633,495 in the comparative quarter) -- modest in absolute terms relative to PAT of 933.92mn, but a genuine FX-translation exposure line, consistent with ASHO importing vehicles/components (Ashok Leyland Limited - India is both the principal supplier, per Note 11.3 -- Purchase of Goods and Other Transactions Rs.3,830,005,537 this quarter -- and a related party); no separate quantification of FX-driven cost impact on Cost of Sales is given elsewhere in the filing (a genuine disclosure gap). No unit sales volume (number of vehicles sold) is disclosed anywhere in this filing -- only Rupee revenue by product line -- a genuine gap flagged per task guidance. cash_from_operations=67,102,512 ('Net Cash Generated from Operating Activities') -- note this is far BELOW 'Operating Profit before Working Capital Changes' of 1,437,091,152 because of a very large working-capital outflow this quarter (Trade and Other Receivables -964,469,234, Amounts due to Related Party -200,827,342, Inventories -695,976,145, partially offset by Trade and Other Payables +606,794,060), consistent with the 110% New Vehicle Sales growth consuming working capital (higher receivables/inventory funding rapid volume growth) -- a genuine and material cash-conversion observation, not an error. capex=50,237,882 ('Acquisition of Property, Plant & Equipment'). cash_from_investing=38,068,527 ('Net Cash Flows Generated from Investing Activities'). cash_from_financing=-1,935,000 ('Net Cash Flows Used in Financing Activities', entirely lease liability payments -- no dividend paid this quarter, unlike the prior full year which paid Rs.72,416,860). Values are stated in absolute Rs. (not Rs.'000 or Rs.mn) as printed in the filing -- unit_scale='1'. Identity check: total_liabilities (8,647,185,861) + total_equity (9,910,635,405) = 18,557,821,266 = total_assets, ties exactly.

interim_updates.note_text: Lanka Ashok Leyland PLC (ASHO) reported Profit After Tax of Rs.933.92mn for Q1 FY2026/27 (three months ended 30 June 2026), up 91.7% YoY from Rs.487.23mn, on Total Revenue of Rs.6,482.22mn, up 99.1% YoY (2025: Rs.3,257.25mn). The growth was driven overwhelmingly by New Vehicle Sales, which more than doubled to Rs.5,950.42mn from Rs.2,831.98mn (+110.1% YoY) and represents 91.8% of Total Revenue this quarter -- the single dominant driver of the result. Spare Parts Sales grew fastest in percentage terms, +166.9% YoY to Rs.193.55mn (2025: Rs.72.51mn), and Vehicle Repair Income grew 14.5% to Rs.93.56mn, but both are small relative to New Vehicle Sales. Vehicle Hiring Income was the only revenue line to decline, -9.7% YoY to Rs.238.69mn (2025: Rs.264.19mn), and Diesel Generator Set Sales fell 12.2% to Rs.6.00mn. Gross Profit rose 81.7% YoY to Rs.1,701.86mn (2025: Rs.936.86mn), with gross margin roughly flat to slightly lower at 26.3% of revenue (2025: 28.8%), meaning Cost of Sales grew slightly faster than revenue (+106.1% YoY to Rs.4,780.36mn vs revenue +99.1%). Administrative Expenses rose sharply, +136.1% YoY to Rs.301.98mn (2025: Rs.127.95mn), and the Impairment Charge on Trade Receivables rose 19.1% to Rs.86.55mn (2025: Rs.72.67mn) -- both scaling with the much larger volume of business but Administrative Expenses in particular grew faster than revenue. Profit before Interest and Tax rose 85.6% YoY to Rs.1,275.33mn (2025: Rs.687.15mn). Net Finance Income (finance income less finance cost) surged 356.5% YoY to Rs.55.89mn (2025: Rs.12.24mn), driven by finance income of Rs.57.92mn (2025: Rs.14.46mn, +300.6%) against a broadly flat finance cost of Rs.2.03mn (2025: Rs.2.21mn, -8.2%) -- this net finance swing added a further Rs.43.64mn to the PBT improvement on top of the operating gain. Profit before Tax rose 90.4% YoY to Rs.1,331.22mn (2025: Rs.699.40mn). Tax Expense rose 87.3% YoY to Rs.397.30mn (2025: Rs.212.17mn), broadly in line with profit growth (effective tax rate 29.8% this quarter vs 30.3% in 2025, essentially stable), so PAT growth (91.7%) tracked PBT growth (90.4%) closely with no material tax drag or benefit. EPS rose to Rs.257.93 from Rs.134.56 (+91.7%), on an unchanged 3,620,843 shares in issue. FX exposure: the cash flow statement shows an unrealised foreign exchange LOSS of Rs.9.17mn this quarter (2025: a small gain of Rs.0.63mn) -- modest relative to PAT but a genuine translation exposure consistent with ASHO's reliance on imported vehicles/ components from related party Ashok Leyland Limited - India (Rs.3,830.01mn of purchases from this related party this quarter, per Note 11.3). Despite the strong profit growth, Net Cash Generated from Operating Activities was only Rs.67.10mn (2025: Rs.631.65mn, a sharp YoY decline) because the 110% New Vehicle Sales growth consumed a large amount of working capital this quarter -- Trade and Other Receivables absorbed Rs.964.47mn of cash and Inventories absorbed Rs.695.98mn, only partially offset by a Rs.606.79mn increase in Trade and Other Payables -- a genuine cash-conversion lag behind the reported profit growth worth monitoring. No unit (vehicle count) sales volume is disclosed in this filing.
interim_updates.gaps_note: No QoQ comparison possible: no quarter closer to 30 June 2026 has been collected for ASHO -- this is the first financial_statements entry for this symbol. No unit sales volume (number of vehicles sold) is disclosed anywhere in this filing -- only Rupee revenue by product line -- a genuine gap per task guidance on capital-goods/vehicle-assembly disclosure. FX exposure is only visible indirectly via the cash flow statement's 'Unrealized Foreign Exchange Loss/(Gain)' adjustment line (Rs.9.17mn loss this quarter); no separate quantification of FX-driven cost impact on Cost of Sales, nor any hedging disclosure, is given elsewhere in the filing. The filing presents a single entity only (no Group/Company distinction, no subsidiaries mentioned) so only one basis (GROUP, by convention) is stored -- there is no separate standalone figure to reconcile against.
interim_updates.takeaway: ASHO's 91.7% YoY PAT growth to Rs.933.92mn was driven almost entirely by New Vehicle Sales more than doubling (+110.1% to Rs.5,950.42mn, now 91.8% of revenue), with a supporting boost from Net Finance Income more than quadrupling to Rs.55.89mn. Gross and operating margins held roughly steady, and the effective tax rate was essentially unchanged, so this was a genuine volume-driven result rather than a margin or tax story. The one caution is cash conversion: operating cash flow fell to just Rs.67.10mn (from Rs.631.65mn a year earlier) as receivables and inventory absorbed cash to fund the sales surge -- worth watching whether this working-capital drag persists as New Vehicle Sales volumes continue to scale, and whether the modest unrealised FX loss (Rs.9.17mn) on imported-component costs grows given the heavy reliance on Ashok Leyland Limited - India as supplier.

operational_highlights: Total Revenue Rs.6,482.22mn, +99.1% YoY (2025: Rs.3,257.25mn); New Vehicle Sales Rs.5,950.42mn, +110.1% YoY, representing 91.8% of Total Revenue this quarter -- the dominant driver.
Spare Parts Sales +166.9% YoY to Rs.193.55mn (fastest-growing line, small base); Vehicle Hiring Income -9.7% YoY to Rs.238.69mn (only revenue line to decline).
Gross margin roughly flat/slightly lower at 26.3% of revenue (2025: 28.8%) as Cost of Sales grew 106.1% YoY, marginally faster than the 99.1% revenue growth.
Administrative Expenses +136.1% YoY to Rs.301.98mn; Impairment Charge on Trade Receivables +19.1% YoY to Rs.86.55mn.
Net Finance Income +356.5% YoY to Rs.55.89mn, driven by Finance Income +300.6% YoY to Rs.57.92mn.
Effective tax rate essentially stable (29.8% vs 30.3% in 2025); PAT growth (91.7%) tracked PBT growth (90.4%) closely.

Net Cash Generated from Operating Activities fell sharply to Rs.67.10mn (2025: Rs.631.65mn) as the New Vehicle Sales surge consumed working capital (Receivables -Rs.964.47mn, Inventories -Rs.695.98mn).

Unrealised FX loss of Rs.9.17mn this quarter (2025: gain of Rs.0.63mn), consistent with ASHO's reliance on imported vehicles/components from related party Ashok Leyland Limited - India (Rs.3,830.01mn of purchases this quarter).
key_drivers: New Vehicle Sales more than doubled YoY (+110.1% to Rs.5,950.42mn, 2025: Rs.2,831.98mn), representing 91.8% of Total Revenue and the overwhelming driver of the 99.1% Total Revenue growth and the resulting 91.7% PAT growth.

Net Cash Generated from Operating Activities fell to Rs.67.10mn from Rs.631.65mn YoY despite profit nearly doubling, because working capital (mainly Trade and Other Receivables, -Rs.964.47mn, and Inventories, -Rs.695.98mn) absorbed cash to fund the New Vehicle Sales volume surge -- a cash-conversion lag worth monitoring alongside the strong headline profit growth.

Net Finance Income +356.5% YoY to Rs.55.89mn (driven by Finance Income +300.6% to Rs.57.92mn) added a further Rs.43.64mn to the PBT improvement, on top of the Rs.588.18mn operating profit improvement.
